study: What should Astra delegate, and does a learned System 1 do that work better than simpler alternatives? (user plan 2026-10-13)
configuration_resolution: Batch 2 used two source configurations: 7 objects (cups A, B, C and dev f1-f4) for its round-2 online runs on dev f1 and f3 and for its section-10 proposal, 11 objects (+ dev g1-g4) for the final leave-one-object-out tables and the round-3 online runs on dev g1 and g4. Those numbers stand as recorded. This study fixes ONE configuration: source = the eight development-family cups (f1-f4, g1-g4); development targets = cups A, B and cylinder C at their recorded bank starts; the development family doubles as additional development targets, each with its OWN records removed from the source selection (effective budget 7/8 of the nominal one); locked evaluation = cup_t1, cup_t2 (never loaded before the prospective batch).
task: adapt the existing grasp-and-lift skill to a new object and the nominal grasp supplied for it (not arbitrary manipulation)
source_record: pre-closing state -> one bounded persistent correction from the bank -> one executed grasp-and-lift -> task-aligned outcome (batch 2's correction banks, rep 0; the labelled positive control is excluded)

selections.rule: for selection k = 0, 1, 2: numpy.random.default_rng(20261014 + k) permutes every source object's records (object order as listed; records ordered by start, then candidate id); budget B takes the first B/8 of every object's permutation, so 16 within 64 within 256; fixed before any target outcome was looked at

candidate_bank_note: nominal + 30 Halton points in the verified per-axis bound +-1.5 cm (object frame), persistent from just before closing through lift and hold (cup_task.PersistentOffset); the development positive control is never selectable or used as data
objective: task-aligned success (batch 2, frozen 2026-10-13): environment lift success, last 30 hold steps >= 4 cm up, upright (up_z >= 0.9), <= 0.10 m/s, and >= 2 fingertip bodies within 2 cm of the object; safety violations reported separately

model.form: locally weighted ridge regression of the outcome on [state features, correction] (s1v2.OutcomeModel, unchanged)
model.support: kernel mass >= mass_min, else unknown with prior q0
model.selection: highest score among admissible candidates; within tie of the best, the smallest correction

representations.none: context-free (A1-A3): the same machinery, no state input
representations.geometry: current + each fingertip body's gap to the outer wall (/R) and height above the base (/H)
representations.post_geometry: exploratory (designed after cup B): fingertip gap/height after translating the pre-closing fingertip positions by the candidate correction, + object size; computed before execution from observed quantities (admissible), see the audit in REPORT.md

retry_rules.no_repeat: a failed candidate is excluded for the rest of the scene (main comparison, A2-A5)
retry_rules.confirm_once: a candidate is excluded after its second failure (experiment C)

update.conservative: target record weight w < 1, chosen on development data (experiment C)

comparisons.question: Was the original grasp simply poorly calibrated?
Does trying a short list provide sufficient adaptation?
Does conditioning on the current state improve selection?
Does feedback-driven updating help beyond moving down a list?
Does updating the contextual model help?
Does context improve how feedback is generalized?
